summary: Rode 47.6 miles from Glenwood Springs to Parachute, CO, a short day. A nail punctured Nunu's tire at the first rest stop, and Drew swapped back tires with her. The team also stopped at an alpaca farm and watched the World Cup third-place game at a sports bar in Rifle.
slept_at: Hotel in Parachute, CO (provided by Olga, Tatiana's mom)
contacts: Olga (Tatiana's mom), hotel in Parachute, CO; she also met the team in Rifle, CO with grandfather Victor
planning_notes: A nail punctured a tire on the Glenwood Springs to Parachute, CO ride. Carry a spare tube and plug kit; a flat sprays sealant everywhere.
Mexican restaurant with a sports bar in Rifle, CO worked as a mid-route meal stop.

summary: Rode 53.5 miles from Parachute to Grand Junction, CO, timed to reach a restaurant with a watch-party room for the World Cup final. The route sent riders onto an overgrown bike path to avoid the Highway 70 tunnel, and they stopped at a Palisade peach stand.
slept_at: Greg and Stephie's home (hosts), Grand Junction, CO
contacts: Greg and Stephie (hosts), Grand Junction, CO
planning_notes: Bikes are not allowed in the Highway 70 tunnel near Grand Junction. The route detours onto an overgrown bike path where branches force riders to unclip; plan around it.
Palisade, CO peach stand has very juicy peaches, a good snack stop.
A Grand Junction restaurant/bar has a watch-party room and free refills of lemonade and iced tea.

summary: Hot ride of 100+ degrees from Grand Junction toward Moab: the team ran out of ice, a driver had to drive back to Grand Junction for more, and riders had mild heat exhaustion. Riders swam in the Colorado River, a storm forced a turn back, and bikes were locked at a campground to finish the next morning. The route file listed 122.5 miles, but the actual ride was 87.9 miles.
slept_at: Moab, UT (team stayed in Moab, see next day)
planning_notes: No ice at any of 5 gas stations within 30 miles on the Grand Junction to Moab route. Carry or pre-buy ice before the 30-mile gap.
Shade is scarce past the Colorado National Monument cliffs; the first shade was a bridge about 60 miles later. Carry extra water for the 28-mile exposed stretch.
Some pickup drivers deliberately tried to run riders off the road on this route. Unintentional drivers are also a real risk.
Sandy, uneven bike path near the Utah welcome sign on I-70 is not safe for a vehicle. A rental minivan with about 3 inches of clearance struggled there.
Gravel road detour near I-70 in Utah filled with dust from passing vehicles for over 30 minutes. Wait it out or avoid it.
Colorado River swim near Moab: strong current and loose rock bed make it hard to stay still. Ride back in the dark only if the road is low traffic.

summary: Rode 32 miles from Hittle Bottom Campground back to Moab, unsupported, to finish the previous day's ride. That evening the team toured Canyonlands at dusk during thunderstorms and flash-flood warnings, found the park mostly empty, and had dinner donated at Arches Thai.
slept_at: Airbnb in Moab, UT (donated by host Margaret)
contacts: Margaret (Airbnb host, Moab, UT), donated the stay
Arches Thai, Moab, UT, donated dinner
planning_notes: Canyonlands visitor center was closed in the evening and the entrance says to pay there. The team used annual National Parks passes, so bring one.
Milt's burger place in Moab is the team's favorite burger; both camps in the team's burger debate agreed on it.

summary: Rest day in Moab. The team visited Arches National Park, hiking Delicate Arch (a hat blew off the trail and was rescued) and Double Arch, then bought metal water bottles at a Moab gear shop after plastic insulated bottles melted their ice. They ate a second burger at Milt's and bought matching shirts.
slept_at: Airbnb in Moab, UT
contacts: Moab gear shop cashier (unnamed), gave a discount on water bottles
planning_notes: Delicate Arch is a 3-mile round trip with switchbacks and exposed slickrock. Go early before the heat, and secure hats, since wind blew one off the trail.
Metal water bottles beat plastic insulated ones in heat; plastic kept ice about 5 minutes. The first Moab shop had only small sizes; the second had full size.
Double Arch is a 0.6 mile path with shade and climbing inside the arch.

summary: Moab to Green River State Park (55.6 miles). The 2026 route swapped I-70 for a gravel road to avoid an 80 mph highway. The driver stopped at Jackass Joe's, an alien-themed gas station at Exit 182 in Crescent Junction, UT, to refill water, and a dirt-road reroute at the highway corner was swamped with mud. The team camped at Green River State Park.
slept_at: Green River State Park campground, UT
contacts: Tamarisk Restaurant, Green River area, UT, donated chilaquiles and French dip subs
Jackass Joe's, Exit 182 Crescent Junction, UT (roadside stop with water and free communal fountain drink)
planning_notes: Spokes 2025 made route files for all 55 days (credited to Joseph Alvarez), with rest stops and pavement notes. The 2026 team built on them. Get those files before routing.
Highway out of Moab toward I-70 near Crescent Junction: 70 mph traffic passes about a foot from riders. The team called it their most dangerous road.
Dirt-road reroute around the I-70 corner near Crescent Junction was completely swamped with mud. Check conditions before sending riders there.
Jackass Joe's is the only water refill near the Crescent Junction corner. Gas is pricey out here, so the driver bought only about 5 gallons.

summary: Driver day for Caroline and Carmen. Riders covered about 95 miles from Green River State Park to Capitol Reef in heat and a thunderstorm wind, with about 13 miles on I-70. Tatiana, Drew and Caroline added extra loops for a century at Capitol Reef.
slept_at: Capitol Reef National Park campground, UT (no showers or laundry)
planning_notes: About 13 miles on I-70 out of Green River with an 80 mph limit. Decent shoulder and light early-morning traffic, so ride early.
Remote Green River to Capitol Reef stretch has few towns. The only town on the route had a cafe with food and wifi. Carry food and water.
Tamarisk (Green River, UT) has a restaurant, a coffee shop that opens at 7 am, and a hotel. Good breakfast and ice stop before the desert.
Capitol Reef campground has no showers or laundry. The team used a hotel in Torrey for showers and the pool.
Afternoon thunderstorm wind hit the final climb into Capitol Reef and lowered morale. Start earlier to avoid it.

summary: Rest day at Capitol Reef: a 5-mile Grand Wash Trail walk and fresh pie at the campground pie shop. A park ranger turned the group back from the scenic drive because of flash-flood warnings. In the evening they went to the Torrey farmers market and the Bicknell International Film Festival's bad-movie screening.
slept_at: Capitol Reef National Park campground, UT
contacts: Tatiana and Noah, hotel in Torrey, UT (used for showers, pool and AC)
planning_notes: Capitol Reef scenic drive was closed to cars during flash-flood warnings. The park's meter went from 'not expected' to 'probable' in one day, so check it before driving park roads.
Capitol Reef campground pie shop makes pies fresh daily; flavors sell out by afternoon.

summary: The trip's biggest climb, about 6,000 ft: from Capitol Reef through red rock, a wind-and-hail squall on a gravel climb, a cold lunch at 9,500 ft, and a 10,049 ft summit in the Dixie National Forest. Steep gravel descents led to a lake stop with kayaks, where two riders ran an hour late with no cell service. The team reached Escalante at dusk.
slept_at: Pastor Richards' home (host), Escalante, UT
contacts: Pastor Richards (host), Escalante, UT; suggested a gravel route, and his dogs Rocky and Mocha
planning_notes: Gravel descents from the Dixie Forest area are very steep. Drew's brakes overheated and stopped working, so check brakes before descents.
Lunch at about 9,500 ft is cold. Bring a rain jacket and warm layer; the team wrapped in blankets.
No cell service on the climbs. Two riders were an hour late and the team could not check on them, so set check-in points.

Escalante to Bryce route: the host suggested a gravel road north of Hwy 12. The team chose the paved highway, the same as the 2025 team, because it had rest stops and a support crew could meet them. The gravel had no Street View and unclear elevation.

summary: Driver day for Drew: Escalante to Bryce Canyon (47.9 miles, about 3,960 ft). The riders faced an 18-mile opening climb, and Drew carried snacks up the hill. The last rest stop was a coffee shop beside a gas station that sells cheeseburgers. Nate's family hosted the team in an Airbnb near Bryce.
slept_at: Airbnb near Bryce Canyon, UT (provided by Nate's family)
contacts: Pastor Richards (host), Escalante, UT; made a protein-heavy breakfast casserole
Mustafa family (Nate's family), Airbnb near Bryce, UT; Nate's dad cooked dinner
planning_notes: Escalante to Bryce opens with an 18-mile climb. Riders ran low on carbs after the protein-heavy breakfast; carry carbs for the climb.
Gas-station cheeseburgers (about $7) at the last rest stop near Bryce, beside a coffee shop.

summary: Rest day at Bryce Canyon with Nate's parents, who cooked meals and brought a birthday cake. The team hiked Sunrise Point and Wall Street (about 2 miles, 600 ft of gain). Dog repellent (pepper spray) leaked in a bike bag, and the residue survived two washes.
slept_at: Airbnb near Bryce Canyon, UT (provided by Nate's family)
contacts: Nate's parents (Mustafa family), Airbnb hosts near Bryce, UT; cooked meals
planning_notes: Sunrise Point and Wall Street hike is about 2 miles with about 600 ft of gain and tight switchbacks. The climb out is hard in heat; bring extra water for anyone who is struggling.
Dog repellent (pepper spray) leaked in a bike bag and its residue survived two washes. Store repellent in a sealed bag away from food.

summary: Bryce Canyon to Zion (100.3 miles, about 4,400 ft). Aarushi and Carmen rerouted the riders onto a Zion backcountry trail that was closed in places. Drew's bike went off a cliff in a rockslide, and he walked it down alone, reaching a shuttle stop after about 2 hours. Caroline's father shuttled four riders through the closed tunnel, and the team regrouped at Zion Lodge that night.
slept_at: Airbnb near Zion, UT (Caroline's family also there)
contacts: Forest (Caroline's dad), drove a van with a bike rack and shuttled four riders through the Zion tunnel
Brady (Caroline's brother), spotted Nate and Nunu at a lookout in Zion
Caroline's grandfather, cooked dinner
planning_notes: Do not reroute onto unfamiliar backcountry trails near Zion. Lodge guides said this trail was impassable by bike and parts were closed. The 2025 team used the road and a car shuttle through the Zion tunnel, which bikes cannot enter.
A trail with Trail Closed, No Trespassing signs and a $5,000 fine had recent collapses. A rockslide took a bike off a switchback.
No cell service in the Bryce-Zion corridor. Set check-in times, and decide in advance when to go look for a late rider.
Zion Lodge vehicle access is gated for shuttle only. Nate and Nunu got in by explaining the situation to security for the code.

summary: Rest day in Zion, with a Walter's Wiggles hike and Angel's Landing summit by Carmen and Aarushi. The team then drove about 3 hours to Las Vegas, where Trek had a replacement bike ready for Drew the same day after several shops did not call back. They returned home around 1 am.
slept_at: Airbnb near Zion, UT
contacts: Trek store, Las Vegas, NV (staff member Chadd), had a bike ready for same-day pickup
Caroline's family, guided the Zion hike
planning_notes: Zion shuttle line at the visitor center was about 30 minutes in the morning. Arrive early for Angel's Landing.
Zion to Las Vegas is about 3 hours by car. Call several bike shops early, since some did not answer.
Driving the Las Vegas Strip took about an hour and finding cheap parking took another hour.

summary: Driver day for Caroline. The Narrows hike was cut short after about 1.5 miles, and Drew and Tatiana could not get through the Zion Lodge car gate. Caroline left early with family. The rest of the team rode from 3 to 10 pm in 100+ degree heat to finish in Cedar City (45.6 miles, about 3,700 ft), with a rider nearly passing out.
slept_at: Airbnb in Cedar City, UT (provided by Carmen's family)
contacts: Carmen's family (Tara and Simone), provided the Cedar City Airbnb
planning_notes: Zion Narrows: rental boots and walking poles cost about $30 each, and more than half the hikers rented them. Start early, around 6 am, to beat the shuttle line.
Heat ride from Zion to Cedar City: gas stations were the only air conditioning and bathrooms. A side road parallel to I-15 cut time on the interstate.
Zion Lodge gate code was not known to the team, so the plan to drive there failed. Confirm the access plan ahead of time.

summary: Cedar City to Milford (59.2 miles, 1,525 ft) in extreme heat. Carmen's twin sister rode until mile 22 and then got a ride back. The team slept inside a Milford church, where showers were hidden behind the chapel stage. Sprinklers hit the team's cowboy camp on the lawn around 12:40 am.
slept_at: Church in Milford, UT (host church; showers behind the chapel stage)
contacts: Milford, UT church hosts (unnamed)
planning_notes: Milford church lawn sprinklers come on around midnight. Cowboy camping there got the team soaked, so sleep indoors or ask the hosts about the schedule.
Scotty's Diner in Milford served good burgers and sandwiches for dinner.

summary: Milford to Baker, NV (84.9 miles, 4,539 ft), crossing into Nevada through long straight desert with climbs and crosswinds. Some riders went to Great Basin National Park for a lake swim, where Nate cut his foot on a sharp rock. The team stayed in a Baker church after dinner at Stargazer Inn.
slept_at: Church in Baker, NV (team slept among the pews)
contacts: Stargazer Inn and Bristlecone General Store, Baker, NV: welcomed the team, served dinner, and suggested the lake hike
Baker, NV church (host, unnamed)
planning_notes: Great Basin lake hike, about 10 minutes from Baker: rocky, uneven trail. Wear closed shoes, not flip-flops. The lake is very cold and muddy, with many bugs. Carry a first aid kit.
Great Basin Visitor Center hosts an evening stargazing talk with telescopes, starting about 8 pm.
Crosswinds on the last 8 miles into Baker: riders drafted in a sideways formation to stay steady.

summary: Drew was too sick to ride. The team called off the Baker to Ely ride (61.7 miles planned) after wildfire smoke reached 'very unhealthy' levels. Nunu drove Drew to Ely, where he ate a burger and recovered. The team stayed at the high school hosting them.
slept_at: High school in Ely, NV (hosting site)
planning_notes: Wildfire smoke in the Baker to Ely valleys reached 'very unhealthy' air quality, and the team cancelled the ride. Check air quality each morning when smoke is visible.
Team's burger ranking (Drew): 1) Milt's, Moab, UT; 2) TJ's Mainstreet Grill, Overbrook, KS, double bacon about $7; 3) Freddy's, Colorado Springs; 4) Dairy Queens in Virginia; 5) In-N-Out.
Carl's Jr. in a gas station across from the Ely high school serves burgers.

summary: Learning festival at an Ely library from 11 am to 5 pm, not the usual 9 to 3; the team had forgotten the schedule. Drew and Nate ran an electric motors workshop, and the team had lunch from a burger place. That evening Nate rode the 36-mile ride skipped the day before, including an 8-mile, 2,000-ft climb, with Nunu driving support.
slept_at: High school library floor, Ely, NV
learning_festival: Ely, NV library, 11 am to 5 pm. About 15 kids signed up, in three groups of five plus a fourth workshop. Activities included an electric motors workshop run by Drew and Nate. Library staff watched kids during lunch, and the city police department ran a festival across the street.
contacts: Ely library staff (LF host; watched kids during lunch)
Ely police department (ran a festival across the street)
planning_notes: Confirm the LF start time with the host. Ely was 11 am to 5 pm, not the usual 9 to 3, and the library was not expecting the team until 11:30.
The van cannot carry five bikes plus LF boxes. Plan bike transport and LF box storage together.
Night ride near Ely: 8 miles and about 2,000 ft climb out of the valley. Very dark with great stars, so bring lights.

summary: Ely to Eureka, NV (79.2 miles, 4,543 ft) on Highway 50. A rear tire popped early on the second stretch, so the support driver had to bring a replacement from Ely. Several riders got sick, and flies swarmed the food at rest stops. The team surprised Nate with a birthday stop. They stayed at a church 18 miles north of the route, reached by shuttle.
slept_at: Church in Eureka, NV (18 miles north of the route, reached by shuttle)
contacts: White Pine County Library staff, Ely, NV: brought breakfast burritos and cinnamon rolls
Church host in Eureka, NV (unnamed)
planning_notes: Carry a spare tube or tire on Highway 50. The replacement tire had to be driven from Ely.
Flies swarmed the food and vehicles at Nevada rest stops. A fly swatter helped.
The Eureka church is 18 miles off the route, so plan a shuttle or van pickup for riders at the end of the ride.

summary: Aarushi's voice-memo day on Highway 50 from Eureka, about 90 miles (3,698 ft), toward Mt. Airy, NV. The day included a sandy cattle-track detour the riders walked, a wrong turn, and a wildfire in the area. The team camped at a church and RV park concrete pad in Austin, NV, and left at 10 pm to ride overnight.
slept_at: Church and RV park campsite (concrete pad), Austin, NV
planning_notes: Highway 50 from Eureka to Austin has about 75 miles with no services. Carry food and water.
The sandy cattle-track detour off Highway 50 was not rideable on bikes; tires sank into the sand. Stay on pavement.
Austin, NV has one restaurant (Grandma's). Pizza took over two hours on a busy night, so call ahead.
Austin campsite: concrete pad, one shower and one outlet shared by the team. Plan charging.
Overnight on Highway 50: cars are visible about 5 minutes out. Calling out 'CAR' and riding single file on the shoulder worked.

summary: Overnight ride on Highway 50 from Mt. Airy to Fallon, NV (about 95 miles, 2,000 ft), starting at midnight. The team pulled over for about an hour of sleep on a tarp at about mile 60 and finished at a Fallon diner for breakfast. Some riders added miles to reach 200 total, and a virus was going around the team.
slept_at: Fallon Youth Club, Fallon, NV (LF host, two nights)
learning_festival: Fallon Youth Club, Fallon, NV: hosts for the final LF, which took place the next day.
contacts: Fallon Youth Club (FYC), Fallon, NV: arranged meals for the team
Fallon diner (unnamed): gave free biscuits and gravy to exhausted riders
planning_notes: Overnight on Highway 50: riders wore white jerseys as capes for visibility, since their dark kit was not reflective. The 'CAR' call and pulling off worked.
A roadside nap of about an hour on a tarp at about mile 60 was possible only because the van was parked as a buffer.
A virus moved through the team (Aarushi, then Drew, then Caroline and Tatiana). Rest when sick.

summary: Final learning festival at the Fallon Youth Club. Most signed-up kids cancelled because of school-supply pickup day, so the team taught one kid in the morning and four in the afternoon (chemistry, Monster Genome, electric motors). The team then donated leftover LF supplies to FYC.
slept_at: Fallon Youth Club Learning Center, Fallon, NV (slept on ottomans and floor)
learning_festival: Fallon Youth Club, Fallon, NV (final LF). Most signed-up kids cancelled for school-supply pickup day. Workshops: chemistry experiment, Monster Genome (felt monsters with traits; kids named theirs), and electric motors run by Drew and Nate. Leftover supplies were donated to FYC.
contacts: Fallon Youth Club (FYC), Fallon, NV: hosted, provided breakfast and dinner, accepted donated supplies
planning_notes: Check the school calendar before scheduling an LF. Mandatory school-supply pickup day in Fallon led nearly all signups to cancel.
Monster Genome and electric motors workshops were the kids' favorites; kids were engaged even with small groups.
Fallon Youth Club is an affordable, grant- and donor-funded aftercare center with a waitlist that prioritizes foster kids and single-parent families. It is a strong LF partner.
Motion-sensor lights in the Learning Center turn on repeatedly overnight. Sleep in another room if possible.

summary: Left Fallon at 2:15 am for South Lake Tahoe (101.4 miles, 5,750 ft). Riders had a sunrise ride, a Carson City coffee-shop stop, and a flat for Drew near the foot of the climb. They climbed about 2,000 ft into South Lake Tahoe, stopped at the California border sign, and reached an Airbnb donated by Nunu's parents.
slept_at: Airbnb in South Lake Tahoe, CA (donated by Nunu's parents)
contacts: Nunu's parents, donated the Airbnb in South Lake Tahoe, CA
planning_notes: Leaving Fallon at about 2 am avoided heat and wind. The sunrise ride had almost no traffic.
The team estimated about 100 tire punctures over the trip. Carry a plug kit and spare tubes.
The Highway 50 California border sign is a good photo stop. The fancier sign nearby is on a trail that was closed for construction.
Carson City stops: a coffee shop with a courtyard and a Wendy's with homestyle potatoes.

summary: Rest day in South Lake Tahoe. The team rented a boat, booked by Nunu's family, for tubing, wakeboarding, a cruise through Emerald Bay, and a swim, and returned it by 3 pm.
contacts: Nunu's family, booked the Tahoe rental boat
planning_notes: Tahoe boat rental: staff gave a safety briefing. The 3 pm return time was firm.
The lake got too choppy for wakeboarding after the first session, so schedule that early.

summary: Rest day in South Lake Tahoe. Drew drove about an hour each way to Reno to replace a blown rear tire at a Trek store. Meanwhile the team was dropped at Sand Beach State Park, where a ranger enforced a no-drop-off zone, a bear walked past an open dumpster, and the group split up without phones. The team cooked a last dinner together, and Drew got second-degree burns from frying burgers in hot oil.
contacts: Trek store, Reno, NV: replaced Drew's blown rear tire
planning_notes: Sand Beach State Park in Lake Tahoe enforces no drop-off at the boat ramp. Arrange pickup from a parking lot.
A black bear walked through the Sand Beach parking lot past an open dumpster. Keep food in the car, not in open bags.
The Trek store is in Reno, NV, not North Lake Tahoe. Verify store addresses first; the drive is about an hour each way.
The group split up with no phones and no meeting plan. Agree on a meeting point and check-in time before separating.
Frying burgers in hot oil caused second-degree burns. Use the grill or oven for big batches.
